parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is nationally uniform: decriminalisation since 2016, constitutional guarantees against torture and sex-based discrimination (Art. 27), and a 2024 hate-crime statute expressly naming gender identity with enhanced penalties — documented positives in force, described as region-leading. No trans-specific criminal offence, entry/document rule, facility restriction, care barrier, police targeting, or violence incident is documented. The gaps are real but are open questions, not exposures: police enforcement practice, screening, facilities, and care for visitors are simply not recorded, and one source's caution that conditions may diverge from statute supplies no incidents. Absence of documented social acceptance (only 'stay vigilant' guidance) and unshown hate-crime enforcement keep this below the acceptance-with-working-protections tier. For solo adults and adults with minors alike, no state-imposed or documented hostility appears.

entry_documents.exposure: No entry, visa, or document-marker rule for trans visitors is documented. No mismatch-friction incident appears.
entry_documents.protection: No documented border protocol; constitutional equal protection applies generally.
entry_documents.interaction: Not documented whether border screening interacts with document mismatch; open question, not an exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented arrest, detention, or custody treatment of trans visitors. Historic s.151 (14 years) repealed 2016.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Constitution Art. 16 bars torture; no trans-specific criminal offence remains.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police enforcement practice against trans people is explicitly listed as undocumented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No bathroom, ward, or facility rule documented at any level. The record explicitly finds no standing subnational variation.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Hate-crime and constitutional protections apply nationally.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Whether facility disputes would arise or be remedied is unmeasured; expectation only, unevidenced.

care_services.exposure: Access to gender-affirming care for travellers is explicitly not documented.
care_services.protection: No documented care denial or medication seizure either.
care_services.interaction: Emergency-care treatment if outed is an open question, not a documented exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No official threat-framing, hostility campaign, or police targeting documented. Travel guidance urges vigilance without citing incidents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Act 13 of 2024 s.5 adds gender identity to protected characteristics with enhanced sentences for hate-motivated violent crime; second jurisdiction in region for comprehensive protection; constitutional non-discrimination (Art. 27) and anti-torture (Art. 16).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Statute is national; whether police invoke it against visitors is not documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: No documented rule, incident, or framing affecting a trans traveller accompanied by a minor.
minors_guardians.protection: Same national hate-crime and constitutional framework applies; no family-specific restriction recorded.
minors_guardians.interaction: No custody, education, or entry interaction for accompanied minors is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence data, killings, or hate-crime enforcement statistics are included; absence is unknown, not safety.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Enhanced prison sentences for GI-motivated violent offences create a formal deterrent and sentencing lever.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: One source warns legal/social conditions can diverge from statute for visitors but names no incidents or locations.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unmeasured divergence between statute and street/official practice is the main open question; no incidents to map it.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional equal protection and non-bailable enhanced hate-crime penalties offer on-paper recourse; repeal and amendments show a functioning legislative channel.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Whether courts and police deliver these remedies to outed visitors is not documented — paper protection, not shown operating.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this case: Vellandra has a documented, routinely enforced border register excluding trans visitors with no remedy. This dossier documents no entry restriction, no registration, no exclusion — only unmeasured unknowns. Known universal exposure versus absent exposure places 0.35-A far below.

Lower than this case: Kestrel Isles documents routine secondary screening, discretionary refusals, and humiliating delays for trans visitors — a documented traveller-facing friction. This dossier records no such screening or refusal practice, only silence, and adds an in-force GI hate-crime statute. Documented friction outweighs undocumented silence.

Close analogue: Vellmaris combines real protections with one documented document-mismatch stop and imperfect rural enforcement. This dossier is slightly higher — no friction incident at all is documented — but similarly lacks evidence that protections operate for visitors, and offers no documented acceptance record either.

Higher than this case: Meridia documents trained border officers, recognised trans passport markers, tribunal appeals with compensation, and counsel access. This dossier has a strong statute but zero documented traveller-facing machinery — no border protocol, no remedy shown working — so it sits a step below.

parsed.synthesis: The documented regime is uniformly favourable on paper: national decriminalisation (2016), constitutional anti-torture and non-discrimination guarantees, and a 2024 hate-crime statute expressly covering gender identity with enhanced penalties — credited as in force. No traveller-facing restriction, targeting, violence, or facility rule is documented at any level of government, and the record finds no subnational variation. The score is held below the top tiers by what is missing rather than by any documented harm: police enforcement practice, border screening, facilities, care, and hate-crime statistics are all explicitly unrecorded, and one source's caution that conditions may diverge from statute supplies no incidents. That is an open question, weighted lightly, but it prevents treating the protections as verified in operation for an outed visitor — solo or with a minor.
